rule: Whole discarded devices and the working modules they usually give. Typical contents, not a promise: a donor's parts are unknown until it is opened and tested. Prices are what was seen on the date given, unopened and untested listings.

capabilities.drive_motors: small DC gearmotors with wheels or tracks
capabilities.high_power_drive: brushless hub motors for a person-sized load
capabilities.wifi_compute: a computer with Wi-Fi that can run an app or a program
capabilities.battery_pack: a ready lithium pack with its protection board
capabilities.charger_5v: a 5 V charger or USB power path
capabilities.stepper_linear: stepper motors, lead screws, rails or belts for straight-line motion
capabilities.router_linux: a network box that can run Linux
capabilities.servo_actuators: position-controlled servos (PWM or bus) for joints and steering
capabilities.submersible_motor: a sealed motor that runs under water (a thruster's starting point)
capabilities.lidar_2d: a spinning 2D laser distance scanner (LDS) for mapping and obstacle range
capabilities.suction_fan: a vacuum suction fan with its rated pressure

devices.name: Android phone with a cracked screen or dead touch, still powers up

gives.camera: rear camera, used through a streaming app
gives.battery_cells: its pouch cell, only inside the phone

hazards: a swollen battery (case bulging, screen lifting): do not charge, do not use, take it to a battery recycling point
first_tests: charges and boots
camera app shows a picture
joins Wi-Fi
Android version: 7.0 or newer runs OpenBot (MIT phone-robot app, minSdkVersion 24); older phones can only stream video
skip_if: Android too old for any streaming app

price_seen.note: an Android 7 Galaxy Note 5 sold as boots and holds a charge: NT$340

devices.name: Robot vacuum without a laser scanner (bump-and-go: Roomba 500-800, Deebot, Thomson, Heran and similar) that powers up but will not run
search_tw: 掃地機器人 零件機

gives.drive_motors_encoded: two drive-wheel modules with gearmotor, encoder and suspension spring
gives.bump_cliff_sensors: front bumper switches and downward floor sensors
gives.battery_pack: its pack, if not worn out
gives.charger_5v: no; it comes with its own dock

interfaces: iRobot Roomba 500 and 600 series take serial commands on a mini-DIN port (iRobot Open Interface); ArduRoomba (MIT, ESP32 support) and PyRoombaAdapter (MIT) speak it
hazards: old NiMH or Li-ion pack: check for leaks or swelling before charging
brush and suction motors draw high current; leave them disconnected
first_tests: each wheel turns by hand and with power
on a Roomba, the Open Interface answers on the serial port
pack voltage under load

price_seen.note: Roomba 571 sold as powers up, will not run: NT$800

devices.name: Xiaomi Mi Robot Vacuum (1st gen SDJQR01RR/02RR, 1S) or Roborock S5/S50/S55/S6 with a fault or dead battery
search_tw: 小米掃地機器人 零件機
米家掃地機器人 故障
石頭掃地機器人 零件機
掃地機器人 雷射頭損壞

gives.lidar_2d: its LDS laser scanner: the LDS02RR on the 1st-gen Mi (kaiaai/LDS lists it as 'Xiaomi Roborock Mi 1st gen'), LDS02RR/LDS01RR on the 1S and Roborock S5/S6; kaiaai/LDS reads it from an ESP32 with an external motor driver
gives.drive_motors_encoded: two drive wheel modules: brushed gearmotor, single-channel Hall encoder, suspension, wheel-drop switch. Measured figures exist for the Roborock S5-family module (OOMWOO part-spec by @IKsares: 65.36:1, 71.5 mm wheel, 2.46 A stall at 14.4 V); whether a 1st-gen Xiaomi's modules match is not verified
gives.suction_fan: a 2-2.5 kPa Nidec 20N704-series suction fan (Roborock S5/S6 family)
gives.battery_pack: BRR-2P4S-5200: 14.4 V Li-ion 4S2P, about 5.2 Ah / 75 Wh, BMS inside the pack, if not worn out
gives.bump_cliff_sensors: front bumper switches and downward cliff sensors

interfaces: Valetudo (Apache-2.0) replaces the cloud firmware on supported Xiaomi/Roborock models: the robot keeps working as a whole, locally controlled
the LDS02RR streams scans over a serial line; kaiaai/LDS (Apache-2.0, Arduino/ESP32) and kaiaai/lds2d (Apache-2.0, Python) decode it
OOMWOO's scanned STEP models give the wheel module (72.7 x 111.2 x 60.4 mm), the LDS02RR (107.7 x 86.5 x 54.1 mm, 76 mm turret) and the pack (44.4 x 142.8 x 43.5 mm); see data/third_party/oomwoo
hazards: Li-ion pack: check for swelling; charge only at 16.8 V CC/CV with the pack's NTC connected (OOMWOO's safety note); the 4-pin connector pinout is unverified
the laser scanner is a Class 1 laser product in its housing; do not open the turret while it runs
suction fan and brush motors draw high current; leave them disconnected while testing the drive
first_tests: on a Xiaomi, 'error 1' means the laser scanner: check its turret spins (its belt and motor are sold separately for about NT$150)
the LDS streams scans to an ESP32 running kaiaai/LDS
each wheel turns and its encoder counts
pack voltage under load
skip_if: main board burnt (smell, scorched area) and the LDS also dead

price_seen.note: 1st-gen Mi Robot (SDJQR01RR/02RR) sold as untested or faulty: NT$1,000, NT$1,900 (unit plus dock), NT$1,999 (error 1), NT$2,625 (laser head broken). A new replacement LDS for Mi 1S/S50/S55 lists at NT$390-736.

devices.name: Neato XV-11/XV-21 or Botvac D-series robot vacuum, faulty or with a dead battery
search_tw: Neato 掃地機器人 故障

gives.lidar_2d: its Neato laser scanner (the XV-11 unit is read by kaiaai/LDS)
gives.bump_cliff_sensors: front bumper switches and cliff sensors

interfaces: kaiaai/LDS (Apache-2.0) lists the Neato XV11 scanner
hazards: older XV packs are NiMH: check for leaks before charging
first_tests: the turret spins and the scanner streams to kaiaai/LDS
skip_if: turret seized and its motor missing

price_seen.note: XV-11 (will not hold charge) NT$1,600; XV-21 NT$2,500; Botvac D-series NT$1,999-3,500

devices.name: Broken toy RC car or tank

gives.drive_motors: one or two small brushed motors with gearbox, wheels or tracks, chassis

hazards: original NiMH or lithium pack may be damaged
first_tests: measure the original battery's voltage: it sets the motors' safe voltage
each motor spins on that voltage
gears not stripped
skip_if: only one motor and you need tank steering

price_seen.note: a new mini tracked tank was NT$396-542

devices.name: Dead laptop battery pack (older, cylindrical-cell packs)

gives.battery_cells: usually 4 to 9 cylindrical 18650 cells; newer packs use flat pouch cells instead

hazards: cutting the case can short or puncture a cell: work slowly, no metal blades into cells
cells below about 2.0 V may be damaged inside: recycle, do not revive
never charge a cell that got hot, smells or is dented
first_tests: resting voltage of each cell
charge in a charger that shows capacity, then measure capacity
self-discharge: voltage after a week

price_seen.note: sold as lots of dead packs

devices.name: Dead or broken power bank

gives.charger_5v: a USB charge and 5 V boost board, if it still works

hazards: swollen pouch cells: recycle
cheap packs may hold fewer or worse cells than labelled
first_tests: cell voltages
does the board still charge and give 5 V

devices.name: Broken self-balancing hoverboard

gives.high_power_drive: two brushless hub motors with tyres and hall sensors

interfaces: hoverboard-firmware-hack-FOC (GPL-3.0) re-flashes many of the original controller boards to take commands over serial; run it as its own program, never copy its code into HS
hazards: 36 V pack holds a lot of energy: a short can start a fire
re-flashing needs an ST-Link and care
first_tests: pack voltage and cell balance
each wheel spins freely
which controller board it has (supported by the open firmware or not)
skip_if: controller board not supported and you cannot drive the motors otherwise

devices.name: Broken inkjet printer or all-in-one

gives.stepper_linear: carriage rod, belt, pulleys, DC motors with optical encoder strips (some have steppers)

hazards: ink is messy; mains supply inside: unplug and wait before opening
first_tests: motor type and voltage from its label
encoder strip intact
skip_if: you need precision: printer DC motors need encoder feedback to position

devices.name: Old flatbed scanner

gives.stepper_linear: a stepper motor, gearbox, smooth rod and belt over the bed length

hazards: glass bed: handle with care
first_tests: stepper coils by resistance

devices.name: DVD or CD drive (computer)

gives.stepper_linear: a tiny stepper with a lead screw and sled (about 4 cm travel)

first_tests: stepper coils by resistance

devices.name: Old Wi-Fi router
first_tests: model is on OpenWrt's supported list
adapter voltage and current from its label
skip_if: not supported by OpenWrt and you need custom software

devices.name: Dead laptop

gives.display: eDP panel (needs a controller board to reuse)
gives.camera: USB webcam module (often usable with a USB lead)
gives.keyboard: a key matrix on a ribbon cable; needs a microcontroller to scan it (no USB on its own)

hazards: battery: see laptop battery pack
panel backlight inverter on old models carries high voltage
first_tests: boots with charger only
webcam module pinout read from the cable or board marking

devices.name: ATX computer power supply

gives.power_supply_mains: 12 V, 5 V and 3.3 V rails with high current; fans

hazards: mains voltage and charged capacitors inside: do not open; use it closed through its connectors only
first_tests: turns on with the green PS_ON wire to ground, output voltages correct under a small load
skip_if: bulging capacitors visible through the vents

devices.name: Broken RC plane, car or robot kit with servos

gives.servo_actuators: micro or standard PWM servos, or serial bus servos in robot kits
gives.drive_motors: car motors; planes give small brushless motors and speed controllers

hazards: LiPo packs in RC models: check for swelling, never charge a damaged one
first_tests: each servo sweeps on its rated voltage with a servo tester or a microcontroller
gears not stripped (no slipping under hand load)
bus servos answer on their serial bus

price_seen.note: used Hiwonder LX-824 bus servos NT$350 each (19 available); broken RC plane NT$400

devices.name: Old USB keyboard

gives.keyboard: works as-is on Linux; its controller board can drive a smaller custom key matrix

first_tests: every key registers

devices.name: Low-voltage aquarium or fountain pump (12 V or USB)

gives.submersible_motor: a sealed low-voltage motor; with the impeller replaced by a propeller it is a common DIY thruster

hazards: mains (110 V) pumps are a different thing: never put one in a model that goes in water with people or as a thruster
first_tests: runs on its rated low voltage
draws its rated current under water

devices.name: 12 V boat bilge pump

gives.submersible_motor: a sealed 12 V motor; DIY underwater drones commonly strip the pump housing and fit a propeller

hazards: draws several amps: fuse it
first_tests: runs on 12 V; current draw in water

devices.name: Microwave oven
hazards: its high-voltage capacitor and transformer can kill even when unplugged; not a salvage donor for HS projects
